section_01.text_05: Building a content department *from the ground up*
section_01.text_06: When I joined Baunfire, a digital agency built for technology companies, there was no content team to lead. As Director of Marketing, Content Strategy and Copywriting, I built one from scratch, grew it into more than $500K in new revenue, and kept writing alongside my team on the client work that mattered most.

section_04.text_02: Baunfire had built its reputation on design and development for technology brands, but content sat outside what it offered. Copy was often handled late in a project or left to clients to write themselves, which meant revenue the agency wasn't capturing and websites that looked sharper than they read.
section_04.text_03: The opportunity was to make content strategy and copywriting a core part of Baunfire's work: a service clients would pay for, a team that could deliver it consistently, and a process that put messaging at the start of every project rather than the end.

section_05.text_02: I owned the department from end to end, from shaping the service offering to hiring, training, and leading the team. I also never stopped writing. On high-stakes engagements like HUMAN Security and WireSafe, I led the strategy and wrote the copy myself, which kept the bar high for the work and showed the team what great looked like on the page.

section_06.text_04: I shaped content strategy and copywriting into services Baunfire could sell, scope, and deliver, so content became part of the pitch instead of an afterthought.
section_06.text_07: I started with trusted freelancers and grew the strongest of them into full-time roles, building a team of writers and strategists who shared the same standards.
section_06.text_10: I created the processes, frameworks, and editorial standards that let the team deliver consistently, and gave thoughtful feedback on the drafts that crossed my desk.
section_06.text_13: I stayed hands-on as a writer, taking on the most demanding client copy myself, so clients got senior-level writing where it counted and the team saw the standard in practice.

section_07.text_03: Many clients were used to treating copy as their own job. I made the case for content strategy in pitches and kickoffs, showing how messaging decisions shaped the design, the performance, and the results.
section_07.text_05: Building quickly can weaken the work, so I scaled the team deliberately and invested in feedback and mentorship to keep every deliverable at the level clients expected.
section_07.text_07: Running a department while writing client copy meant protecting time for both. Clear frameworks let the team move independently, which freed me to write where my experience mattered most.

section_10.text_01: “Nicole didn’t just step into a role; she built an internal content and strategy team from the ground up… She is a rare combination of killer strategist, empathetic writer, thought-provoking editor, and patient leader.”
section_10.text_02: **Robin Noble**, Content & SEO Strategist, Baunfire · on Nicole’s team, first as a freelancer and then full time

section_11.text_01: “She led strategy and copy for web projects with clarity, creativity, and intention… a true partner in the creative process, always bringing insights and a strong point of view.”

section_13.text_01: The best way to build a writing team is to keep writing.
section_13.text_02: Building the department taught me that leadership and craft aren't separate tracks. Staying close to the work kept my feedback specific and my standards credible, and it gave the team a clear picture of what we were all aiming for.
section_13.text_03: It's why I still lead from the page, whether I'm guiding a team of writers or drafting a homepage myself.
